comment:
* Extension of TextView that can handle displaying and inputting a range of * numbers. *

* Clients of this view should never call {@link #setText(CharSequence)} or * {@link #setHint(CharSequence)} directly. Instead, they should call * {@link #setValue(int)} to modify the currently displayed value.

variables.name: mMaxCount
variables.comment: Number of digits in the maximum value.

variables.name: mCount
variables.comment: Number of digits entered during editing mode.

variables.name: mPreviousValue
variables.comment: Used to restore the value after an aborted edit.

methods.name: protected void onFocusChanged(boolean focused, int direction, Rect previouslyFocusedRect)
public final void setValue(int value)
methods.comment:
* Sets the currently displayed value. *

* The specified {@code value} must be within the range specified by * {@link #setRange(int, int)} (e.g. between {@link #getRangeMinimum()} * and {@link #getRangeMaximum()}). * * @param value the value to display

methods.name: public final int getValue()
methods.comment:
* Returns the currently displayed value. *

* If the value is currently being edited, returns the live value which may * not be within the range specified by {@link #setRange(int, int)}. * * @return the currently displayed value

methods.name: public final void setRange(int minValue, int maxValue)
methods.comment:
* Sets the valid range (inclusive).
     *
     * @param minValue the minimum valid value (inclusive)
     * @param maxValue the maximum valid value (inclusive)

methods.name: public final void setShowLeadingZeroes(boolean showLeadingZeroes)
methods.comment:
* Sets whether this view shows leading zeroes. *

* When leading zeroes are shown, the displayed value will be padded * with zeroes to the width of the maximum value as specified by * {@link #setRange(int, int)} (see also {@link #getRangeMaximum()}. *

* For example, with leading zeroes shown, a maximum of 99 and value of * 9 would display "09". A maximum of 100 and a value of 9 would display * "009". With leading zeroes hidden, both cases would show "9". * * @param showLeadingZeroes {@code true} to show leading zeroes, * {@code false} to hide them

methods.name: private void updateDisplayedValue()
methods.comment:
* Computes the display value and updates the text of the view. *

* This method should be called whenever the current value or display * properties (leading zeroes, max digits) change.

methods.name: private void updateMinimumWidth()
methods.comment:
* Computes the minimum width in pixels required to display all possible * values and updates the minimum width of the view. *

* This method should be called whenever the maximum value changes.
